The consolidated figure (1,247.55 crore, line 28858) nets shares held by subsidiaries; the higher count is used. Held flat: no SBC, no buybacks, no planned equity raise.

inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows. Risk-free ~6.8% (India 10-year G-sec), equity risk premium ~7% including India country risk, levered beta ~1.15 for an integrated steel producer -> cost of equity ~14.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~8.2%, after tax ~6.1%. Capital weights on market values: net debt INR 914bn against ~INR 2.33tn market cap = ~28% debt. WACC = 0.72 x 14.8% + 0.28 x 6.1% = ~12.4%, set at 12.0% because ~a third of revenue (not of profit) is funded in lower-rate GBP/EUR. The same 12% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, Dutch regulatory risk and UK execution risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once). Terminal growth 5% is INR nominal (~4% inflation plus ~1% real), well below India nominal GDP growth.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. The company's own gross debt figure (INR 102,368 crore at 30 Sep 2026) includes lease liabilities (FY2026: INR 7,425 crore), so they are deducted once in net debt; lease principal (INR 1,162 crore in FY2026) is NOT deducted from the flows and EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116. lease_cost_pct_path is therefore zero.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); non-controlling interests are deducted once in the equity bridge at FY2026 book value (INR 1,612.80 crore). NCI is under 2% of total equity, so book value is a reasonable proxy.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company-reported net debt at 30 Sep 2026 (2QFY27 results presentation, slide 22): gross debt INR 102,368 crore including leases, less cash, bank balances and current investments INR 10,301 crore, less MTM gain on currency hedges INR 644 crore = INR 91,423 crore. 'cash' here carries the 10,301 plus the 644 hedge gain so that total_debt - cash ties to the reported net debt. Net debt rose from INR 80,144 crore at 31 Mar 2026 during H1 on a working-capital build, INR 6,860 crore capex and the INR 4,989 crore dividend.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Tata Steel is an integrated steel operating company whose value is an unlevered free cash flow stream; it is not a bank, REIT, holdco or distressed shell. First valuation of this ticker (fresh build, no reconciliation). CYCLICALITY: drivers are mid-cycle, not extrapolated from a single year. Company-definition EBITDA margin ran 26.2% (FY22 peak), 13.4%, 10.2% (FY24 trough), 11.8%, 15.0% (FY26) and 15.9% in 1H FY27; the base case settles at 17% reflecting the mix shift toward India (~25-26% margin) and the end of UK blast-furnace losses, not a return to FY22. The Metrics CSV EBITDA (INR 361bn FY26, 15.6%) includes other income and runs ~0.5pp above the company definition. YEAR 1 is FY2027, anchored to 1H FY27 actuals (revenue INR 126,231 crore, EBITDA INR 20,035 crore). TIMING: net debt is at 30 Sep 2026 while year-1 flows are the full FY2027; H1 unlevered FCF was slightly negative (working-capital build), so the overlap does not flatter value. FY2026 reported FCF of INR 205bn contained a ~INR 35bn working-capital release that reversed in H1 FY27 and is not a run-rate; the component-built year-1 owner FCF is ~INR 130bn. DEBT HISTORY: total_debt for FY2016-FY2020 in the Metrics CSV is understated (current maturities sat in other financial liabilities before the 2021 Schedule III change); leverage is anchored on the company's own FY2022-1H FY27 gross/net debt series only. NOT IN THE BRIDGE: equity-accounted investments and any residual pension surplus/deficit (immaterial against INR 914bn net debt); UK and Dutch government grants are treated as reducing net capex inside capex_pct_path. SBC-zero: house and street values coincide and the band collapses (band_position not meaningful). Price is a regular-session print, not after-hours. No buybacks have ever been made; the flat share count needs no funding.

equity_bridge.note: FY2026 consolidated balance sheet, INR 1,612.80 crore (TATASTEEL.NS_Annual_FY2026.txt:24821)

historical_growth.notes: FY2026 against FY2023 (3yr) and FY2021 (5yr). Owner FCF equals reported FCF (no SBC; interest income not stripped because the company is in net debt). Point-to-point CAGRs are cycle artefacts for a steel producer: FY2021 FCF was a working-capital-release peak (INR 373bn) and FY2023 a weak year (INR 75bn), so the FCF CAGRs carry no signal. The 3-year revenue and equity CAGRs are negative because FY2023 still carried peak steel prices and FY2024 took UK restructuring impairments. The 10-year revenue CAGR (FY2016-FY2026) is 8.1%. Forward growth is built from India volume additions and mid-cycle pricing, cross-checked against the 6.6% five-year equity CAGR.

base.growth_note: Year 1 (FY2027) annualises 1H FY27 revenue of INR 126,231 crore with a seasonally stronger H2. Later years: India volumes from Kalinganagar Phase II ramp and the NINL 4.8 MTPA expansion (~FY2029-30), mid-cycle realisations, flat-to-lower European volumes.
base.margin_note: 1H FY27 actual 15.9% (company definition). Rises to 17.5% as India share grows and UK blast-furnace losses end with the Port Talbot EAF (late 2027/2028), then settles at a 17% mid-cycle level. Ten-year average is ~16%.
base.capex_note: FY2026 actual 6.3% of revenue; FY2027 guided around INR 20,000 crore with INR 6,860 crore spent in H1. 7.5% through the NINL / UK EAF / Dutch decarbonisation years (net of grants), gliding to 6.0% against D&A of 5.3% in a business still growing 5% nominal.
base.tax_note: Applied to consolidated EBIT. India statutory 25.17%; the consolidated rate runs higher because European losses are not shielded. FY2026 cash tax INR 46bn was ~27% of pre-tax profit. Interest tax shield is in the WACC, not the flows.
base.wc_note: Negative: an integrated steel producer's inventories and receivables exceed payables, so revenue growth consumes cash (~10% of incremental revenue).

scenario_narratives.base: India carries the group. Kalinganagar Phase II ramps and the NINL expansion adds volume toward the end of the decade, India holds a ~24-26% EBITDA margin on captive iron ore, and the consolidated margin drifts from 16% to a 17% mid-cycle level as India's share of the mix rises and the Port Talbot EAF ends UK blast-furnace losses from FY2029. The Netherlands stays a thin-margin business that reaches a negotiated decarbonisation deal with meaningful state support. Capex stays heavy (7-7.5% of revenue) through FY2030 before easing to 6%. Steel prices are mid-cycle: neither the FY2022 spread nor the FY2024 trough. Net debt declines slowly from INR 914bn.
scenario_narratives.bull: An Indian steel upcycle: demand compounds 8-9% a year on infrastructure and housing, the safeguard duty is extended beyond April 2028, and Chinese exports recede as capacity is curtailed. India margins hold in the high twenties, Tata reaches its 40 MTPA ambition on schedule, the Port Talbot EAF commissions on time and turns the UK cash-positive, and IJmuiden gets a funded transition without forced early closure of the coke and gas plants. Consolidated margin reaches 19.5% -- still well short of the 26% FY2022 peak -- and deleveraging accelerates.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle turns while the balance sheet is still carrying INR 900bn of net debt. Chinese exports stay above 100 Mt, India's safeguard duty lapses in 2028 and domestic realisations fall, coking coal stays elevated, and the consolidated margin drops back to the 12% range seen in FY2024-25 before recovering only to 14%. The Dutch regulator forces early closure of the IJmuiden coke and gas plants, pushing Tata Steel Nederland into losses and raising closure and remediation spend; the UK EAF slips and Llanwern is squeezed by quota-free imports. Capex cannot be cut much because the projects are mid-build, so free cash flow thins and debt stops falling.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default: net debt of 2.4x EBITDA on a commodity margin, a single-regulator dependency at IJmuiden (permit revocation notice, court hearing 20 November 2026) and an India safeguard duty that expires in April 2028. Base 50%: the India expansion is largely built or under construction and 1H FY27 is tracking it. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs several independent things to go right at once -- a sustained Indian upcycle, continued trade protection, on-time UK EAF commissioning and a benign Dutch outcome.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A leveraged cyclical valued on mid-cycle unlevered cash flow in INR, with the cycle, the Dutch regulatory risk and UK execution carried in three scenarios rather than in the discount rate. Because ~INR 914bn of net debt sits ahead of the equity, small changes in mid-cycle margin move per-share value disproportionately: the spread between bear and bull is the main finding, not the point estimate. The terminal value is capped at 14x owner FCF (Gordon at 12%/5% gives 15x), which equates to roughly 5-6x terminal EBITDA -- in line with where integrated steel producers have traded through the cycle and below the ~8x forward EV/EBITDA the Indian market pays today.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle EBITDA margin: each 1pp on the terminal margin is worth roughly INR 12-15 per share because of the debt ahead of the equity
Capex intensity after FY2030: the base case assumes it eases to 6% of revenue; a 40 MTPA build-out plus European decarbonisation could keep it at 7%+
IJmuiden coke and gas plant permits: forced early closure would bring closure costs and losses not fully captured outside the bear case
India safeguard duty expiry (April 2028) and Chinese export volumes
Port Talbot EAF commissioning (late 2027/early 2028) and the UK's cash burn until then
Discount rate: the Indian market currently capitalises domestic steel earnings at a lower implied rate than the 12% used here; the required-return table shows what the price implies
